# WLMAC Robotics

> Student-run FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) robotics program at William Lyon Mackenzie Collegiate Institute in North York, Toronto, Ontario. Two teams: CyberLyons (FTC #27964, founded 2024) and MechLyons (FTC #32514, founded 2025). Funded by partners and donations; donations go through the Toronto District School Board and get a tax receipt.

- Website: https://wlmacrobotics.ca/
- Email: hello@wlmacrobotics.ca
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/wlmac.ftc/
- Donate (TDSB, Robotics initiative pre-selected): https://tdsb.schoolcashonline.com/Fee/Details/457/153/false/true?school=599&initiative=75

## Key facts
- 6+ FTC competitions in the 2025/26 season, including a Toronto qualifier in February 2026
- 7 free Arduino workshops, May to August 2026, for 195 kids aged 5 to 18
- Season budget: about $10,000 CAD for both teams
- Partners: IEEE, kama.ai, SAVI, XK Innovate, Meritus Academy, Jukebox Print, Fabworks
- No sponsorship tiers in 2026/27: every partner gets their logo on the website and an end-of-season report

## FAQ
### What is WLMAC Robotics?
WLMAC Robotics is the student-run FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) program at William Lyon Mackenzie Collegiate Institute in North York, Toronto. It fields two teams: CyberLyons (#27964, founded 2024) and MechLyons (#32514, founded 2025). Students design, machine, code and drive every robot themselves.

### What is FIRST Tech Challenge?
FIRST Tech Challenge is an international robotics league where student teams design and build 18-inch robots for a new game each year, then compete in alliances against other teams.

### How can a business support the team?
Donate any amount, give parts, tools, machine time or services, or mentor a student. There are no tiers and no minimum: every partner gets their logo on this website and a short end-of-season report showing where their support went.

### Do donations get a tax receipt?
Yes. Donations go through the Toronto District School Board (TDSB), a registered charity, which emails a tax receipt after checkout. Businesses should pay with the company card and enter the business name in the name fields so the receipt is in the company's name.

### How do I donate?
Use the TDSB online donation page, which is already set to William Lyon Mackenzie CI and the Robotics initiative. Pick any amount, skip the Tribute section, and check out as a guest. You can also mail a cheque payable to "TDSB-William Lyon Mackenzie CI" to the school.

### Can my logo go on the robot or team shirts?
Not this season. Our main partner already holds the robot and team shirt space, so every other partner's logo goes on our website instead.

### Where does the money go?
A season for both teams costs about $10,000 CAD: FTC registration and event fees, robot parts and electronics, fabrication materials, tools, travel, and supplies for free community workshops.

### What outreach does the team do?
From May to August 2026 the team ran seven free Arduino workshops for 195 kids aged 5 to 18 with North York Community House, Joyce Public School, Dublin Heights E&MS and Human Moves Camp. It also brings robots to the Mackenzie Science and Engineering Olympics, Grade 9 Night and the Library Open House.
